findings.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) but GoogleCalendarService stores that envelope directly as the credential key via data: { key }, replacing the schema-shaped credentials the old googleCredentialSchema.parse stored. On the default path (sharing disabled), the first Google token refresh persists key = {success: true, data: {...}}; the next GoogleCalendarService construction runs googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) on the envelope, throws ZodError, and every Google Calendar availability check and booking fails for that user until they manually reconnect — the stored refresh_token is also nested under data, so the credential is effectively destroyed.

[BUG] The computed schema keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal property name "[object Object]" (zod schema objects have no custom toString), so minimumTokenResponseSchema is actually {access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown} — it neither matches 'any numeric property as expiry' nor 'allows other properties', and z.object's strip mode drops every real field except access_token. With credential sharing enabled, every provider's refresh response is stripped to {access_token}: office365 loses expires_in (stale expiry forces a refresh on every call), zoom loses expires_in, and salesforce — which always calls Salesforce directly yet parses with this schema when sharing is on — persists a key missing instance_url/signature/id, so the next jsforce.Connection is built with instanceUrl undefined and all Salesforce API calls fail.

[BUG] When the parsed data lacks refresh_token, the function writes the literal string "refresh_token" into data.refresh_token — a placeholder, not a token — and callers persist it. Under the sharing path the broken minimum schema always strips refresh_token, so Office365CalendarService spreads {refresh_token: "refresh_token"} over o365AuthCredentials and prisma persists it, permanently destroying the real Microsoft refresh token and forcing every affected user to reconnect; zoom's refreshed credential is corrupted the same way, and any provider response that legitimately omits refresh_token now corrupts the stored credential instead of preserving the old value as the previous spread-only code did.

[BUG] The sharing branch returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT while all nine call sites expect the provider-specific shape that refreshFunction returns. With sharing enabled the feature crashes or corrupts at every call site: Google reads res?.data (undefined on a Response) and throws TypeError reading access_token; Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read tokenInfo.data.error and throw TypeError; Hubspot stores undefined token fields with a NaN expiry; Lark feeds the non-Lark body to handleLarkError which rejects it — the credential-sync feature cannot function as shipped.

[BUG] The added block performs an eager, unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation — not gated on token expiry and not routed through refreshOAuthTokens — and any failure (non-OK status, network error, schema mismatch) rejects the connection promise. Every Salesforce calendar operation now pays an extra OAuth round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a DB write, and operations that previously succeeded with the stored access token now hard-fail at construction time whenever the refresh endpoint hiccups, turning a lazy refresh into a per-operation outage.

[BUG] salesforceTokenSchema requires scope: z.string(), but Salesforce's refresh-token grant response returns access_token, signature, instance_url, id, issued_at and token_type with no scope field, so parseRefreshTokenResponse throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' on every refresh. On the default path (no sharing env vars), the now-unconditional refresh in the constructor fails schema validation on every instantiation, so the Salesforce integration stops working entirely for every user after this change.

[BUG] zoho-bigin passes credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' third argument, which every other call site populates with credential.userId and which the helper sends as calcomUserId in the sync request. The credential-sync endpoint receives a credential id where it expects a Cal.com user id, resolves the wrong user (or none), and refreshed tokens are synced against the wrong account; if no local credentialId is in scope this reference additionally breaks the build since the class stores the value as this.credentialId.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds three behavior-bearing modules — parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens, and the app-credential webhook endpoint — with no test anywhere in the diff exercising any of them. The exact defect class this diff ships (the safeParse envelope persisted as a credential key in GoogleCalendarService, the '[object Object]' computed schema keys, the literal refresh_token placeholder) would be caught by one unit test asserting the persisted key shape or the parsed output, so the next refactor of this path regresses the same way; a regression here breaks OAuth refresh for seven integrations at once.

[ADVISORY] The handler validates input with throwing APIs inside no try/catch — appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws ZodError on malformed bodies and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws on undecryptable or non-JSON payloads — and it never checks req.method. The parent application sending a malformed, wrongly-encrypted, or non-JSON payload (or a GET request) gets an opaque Next.js 500 with a stack trace instead of a 4xx, leaving no error contract for the operator to debug why credential sync failed.

[ADVISORY] The webhook secret — the sole authentication for an endpoint that can overwrite any user's credentials — is compared with a plain !== string comparison rather than crypto.timingSafeEqual. The comparison early-exits on the first differing byte, leaking a timing side channel that lets an attacker who can measure response times recover the secret and then inject arbitrary credential keys for any userId in the request body.

[ADVISORY] The outbound sync request sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header and no timeout, even though the reverse direction (parent app to Cal.com) is authenticated with CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The parent application cannot verify the request came from its Cal.com instance, so anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT requests fresh access tokens for arbitrary users unverified; and a slow or hung parent app stalls the token refresh — which runs inside booking and availability flows — until undici's multi-minute socket timeouts fire.

[ADVISORY] The header lookup uses process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME verbatim while Node lowercases all incoming header names, so an operator who configures a mixed-case value (e.g. 'Calcom-Webhook-Secret') gets a silent mismatch. Every credential-sync webhook then returns 403 'Invalid webhook secret' — a misleading message that sends the operator debugging their secret instead of their header-name casing — and the one-call fix (lowercasing the env value before lookup) is absent.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted keys object is persisted as credential.key without being validated against the target app's credential schema (e.g. googleCredentialSchema) before the 200 is returned. A parent-app bug that pushes a key missing refresh_token or access_token bricks the user's integration at the next service construction (the schema parse throws) while the webhook returns 200 'Credentials updated', so the parent app never learns it shipped a broken credential.

[BUG] GoogleCalendarService persists the Zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse directly as credential.key instead of the parsed credential data. The first Google token refresh after this deploy overwrites the stored credential with {success: true, data: {...}}; the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) (no access_token/refresh_token at the top level), so every Google Calendar operation - booking creation, updates, availability - throws for that user until they manually re-authorize the app.

[BUG] In credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, and the code reads res?.data - a property fetch Response does not have - so token is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Any self-hoster with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set gets 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)' on every Google Calendar token refresh, failing all Google calendar operations in the exact configuration this PR exists to support.

[BUG] In sharing mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, and `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` dereferences Response.data which is undefined, throwing TypeError. Under credential sync every Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)', so Bigin calendar operations fail for self-hosters using the sync endpoint.

[BUG] In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, and `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` dereferences the undefined Response.data, throwing TypeError. Under credential sync every Zoho CRM token refresh crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)', breaking Zoho CRM calendar operations in sharing mode.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the literal string 'refresh_token' into the parsed credential data whenever the response lacks a refresh_token - which is every response in sharing mode, because minimumTokenResponseSchema strips all unknown keys from its output. O365's spread `o365AuthCredentials = {...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)}` and Zoom's subsequent credential update replace the user's real refresh token with the unusable literal and persist it, so the integration dies with invalid_grant on the next direct refresh (for example the moment the operator disables the sync endpoint) and the user must re-authorize.

[ADVISORY] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug - no authentication header or shared secret - even though the inbound webhook this feature pairs with requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET on every request. The operator's sync endpoint hands out live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user IDs but has no way to verify the caller: anyone with network access to it can mint valid access tokens for any user, and nothing in .env.example warns that the endpoint must be network-isolated.

[BUG] The computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the same junk string ('[object Object]', the second overwriting the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema implements neither the 'any numeric property is the expiry' rule nor 'allow other properties' - it is effectively z.object({access_token: z.string()}) that strips every other field from its parsed output. In sharing mode all token fields except access_token are silently discarded before persistence: O365 never receives the new expires_in so the credential's expiry never advances (refresh runs on every operation), and Salesforce's stored key is stripped to {access_token, refresh_token}; no expiry validation ever runs, so any sync response with a string access_token passes.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds an authenticated credential-writing webhook endpoint, two mode-switching OAuth utilities (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse), and a rewritten Salesforce token flow, yet contains zero test files - none of the touched paths matches spec/test patterns. The regressions this diff ships - Google persisting the Zod safeParse envelope as the credential key and the sharing-mode Response/.data TypeErrors in three apps - are precisely what a unit test asserting parseRefreshTokenResponse's return shape and refreshOAuthTokens' sharing-mode contract would have caught; every future refactor of this path ships blind.

[BUG] The handler performs no req.method restriction and calls the throwing zod .parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse with no try/catch, so every malformed input becomes an unhandled exception. The parent application receives an opaque HTTP 500 instead of a 4xx for a GET with a valid secret (req.body is undefined, .parse throws ZodError), a body missing required fields, or a payload encrypted with a rotated CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, leaving the operator unable to distinguish their own payload bug from a Cal.com server fault.

[ADVISORY] The connection setup now performs an unconditional token refresh - a fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma credential write - on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where the previous code created the jsforce Connection lazily and refreshed only when an API call actually needed a new token. Every booking operation touching a Salesforce calendar now incurs a synchronous round-trip to Salesforce and a DB write, burns Salesforce token-endpoint rate limits, and fails outright whenever Salesforce's token endpoint hiccups even though the stored access token is still valid - converting a transient Salesforce outage into total Salesforce unavailability.

[BUG] zoho-bigin passes credentialId (the credential row's id) as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter, unlike every sibling call site in this diff which passes credential.userId. Under credential sync the request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries calcomUserId=<credential id>, so the parent application looks up the wrong user or none at all and returns the wrong user's tokens or an error, breaking Zoho Bigin refresh even when the sync setup is otherwise correct.

[BUG] The sharing-mode return of refreshOAuthTokens - a raw fetch Response - is assigned to a HubspotToken-typed variable and consumed as a Hubspot token, so every field the following code reads (access_token, expires_in, refresh_token) is undefined. Under credential sync the Hubspot refresh computes a NaN expiry_date and persists a credential with undefined access_token, so every subsequent Hubspot API call fails authentication until the user re-authorizes.

[BUG] The new Salesforce refresh path never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, so the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED / CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT gating that every other app in this diff honors is silently unchecked here, while parseRefreshTokenResponse still switches to the stripping minimum schema when sharing is on. A self-hoster running credential sync still must hold real Salesforce client secrets and per-user refresh tokens inside Cal.com (sync is unimplemented for Salesforce), and in sharing mode the persisted key is stripped to {access_token, refresh_token} - losing instance_url, id and signature - so subsequent jsforce connections target the wrong host and Salesforce operations fail.

[BUG] In sharing mode the value passed to handleLarkError is the sync contract {access_token, expiry}, which lacks Lark's required code/msg/data envelope, so the Lark-shape validation rejects it (or yields undefined nested data). Under credential sync every Lark token refresh throws, so Lark calendar operations fail for self-hosters using the sync endpoint.

[BUG] In sharing mode responseBody is the sync contract {access_token, expiry}, but the adapter consumes Webex-specific fields (refresh_token, expires_in) that this contract never contains. Under credential sync the Webex adapter persists a credential with undefined refresh_token and a NaN expiry, so meetings fail once the first access token expires and the credential can never be refreshed again.

[BUG] In sharing mode the response handed to handleErrorsJson<ITokenResponse> is {access_token, expiry}, missing the expires_in/refresh_token/token_type fields the MS Teams adapter reads from it. Under credential sync the Teams adapter computes a NaN expiry and persists undefined token fields, triggering a refresh attempt on every call and failing meeting creation once the stale access token expires.

[BUG] The header lookup uses process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME verbatim without lowercasing it, while Node lowercases all incoming header names. An operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME to any mixed-case value (e.g. 'Calcom-Webhook-Secret') gets undefined on every lookup and a permanent 403 'Invalid webhook secret' that misattributes the failure to the secret itself; only a prose comment in .env.example hints at the constraint.

[BUG] The findFirst-then-create sequence runs without a transaction and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent syncs both take the create path, and the unordered findFirst thereafter updates a nondeterministic row. Overlapping initial syncs create duplicate credentials for the same user and app, and later syncs update only one of them, leaving a stale credential that booking flows can still select - producing intermittent 401s that survive every re-sync.

[BUG] The decrypted keys JSON is persisted as credential.key without any schema validation, so any decryptable-but-wrong payload (a string, null, or an object missing the app's required fields) is stored and acknowledged with 200 'Credentials updated'. The parent app believes the sync succeeded while the user's integration is bricked - the app's service constructor throws on the malformed key at the next booking - and no error surfaces at sync time to tell the operator their payload shape is wrong.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod safeParse result ({success, data}), and this call site stores that wrapper object directly as credential.key instead of the parsed credential. In the default (non-sharing) configuration, the first Google token refresh overwrites credential.key with {success:true, data:{...}}; every subsequent read of credential.key.access_token / .refresh_token returns undefined, so all Google Calendar operations fail and every Google-connected user must re-authenticate — persistent credential corruption for all deployments.

[BUG] In credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this call site reads res?.data — a gaxios-only shape that does not exist on a fetch Response — so token is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google token refresh crashes in sharing deployments, so the sync feature breaks the very integration flow it was built for; Google Calendar is unusable whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set.

[BUG] Both computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (ZodString does not override toString), so the second entry overwrites the first and the "minimum" schema requires only access_token — the intended "any property with a number is the expiry" validation does not exist. Sharing mode accepts token responses with no expiry field at all, so callers store undefined expiry_date/expires_in into credentials; tokens are then treated as expired on every use (or mis-handled per app), and the documented validation invariant of the feature is never enforced.

[BUG] The util unconditionally injects the literal string "refresh_token" as data.refresh_token whenever the parsed response lacks one — which is every response in sharing mode, since the sync endpoint returns only access token and expiry — and callers persist that value to the credential table. Every synced app's stored credential carries a fake refresh token; any downstream missing-refresh_token guard (e.g. zoom's) now passes on garbage, and if sharing is later disabled the direct-refresh path sends refresh_token="refresh_token" and the integration fails permanently until re-auth.

[BUG] The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header — CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is never attached — even though the inbound webhook at apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts rejects callers without that same secret. The parent app's endpoint must serve live OAuth access tokens unauthenticated, so anyone with network access to it can enumerate calcomUserId values and harvest valid access tokens for every app slug; the feature's shared-secret invariant is enforced on only one leg of the exchange.

[BUG] The service now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a credential DB write on every SalesforceCalendarService construction — previously the jsforce connection refreshed lazily — and this new flow never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, so it is disconnected from the credential-sync feature the PR claims to implement. Every Salesforce availability check and booking now makes a synchronous login.salesforce.com round-trip and a DB write even when the stored access token is valid, adding latency to the booking hot path and multiplying token-endpoint load; the change is also implementation work not traceable to any stated requirement.

[BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse bypasses salesforceTokenSchema and zod's default strip behavior reduces accessTokenParsed.data to {access_token} (plus the injected sentinel), so the credential update persists {access_token, refresh_token} and drops instance_url, signature, id, issued_at, scope and token_type. After the first refresh in a sharing deployment the stored Salesforce credential has no instance_url, so every subsequent jsforce connection targets the wrong endpoint and the Salesforce integration breaks until the user re-authenticates — enabling sharing for any other app corrupts Salesforce credentials.

[BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but line 96 reads tokenInfo.data.error and a fetch Response has no data property, so the expression throws TypeError (reading 'error' of undefined). Every zoho-bigin token refresh fails in sharing deployments, so Bigin calendars stop working as soon as the credential-sync env vars are configured.

[BUG] In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and reading .error on it throws TypeError. Every Zoho CRM token refresh fails in sharing deployments, breaking Zoho CRM calendars whenever the sync feature is enabled.

[BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response that is assigned to the HubspotToken-typed variable, so .access_token, .refresh_token and .expires_in are all undefined when the new credential is computed and persisted. Hubspot stores a credential with undefined tokens and a NaN expiry_date, silently breaking the integration in sharing deployments with no error at refresh time — failures surface later as confusing 401s.

[BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips the zoom response to {access_token} plus the injected sentinel refresh_token:"refresh_token", and this stripped result is persisted as the credential key. The stored zoom credential loses token_type, scope and expires_in and carries a junk refresh token; if sharing is disabled or the endpoint removed, zoom refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" and the integration fails permanently until the user reinstalls the app.

[BUG] The spread ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) merges the injected sentinel refresh_token:"refresh_token" over the credential's real refresh_token and the merged object is persisted via prisma.credential.update. In sharing mode every office365 refresh destroys the real refresh token in the DB; disabling sharing later (or a team credential with null userId falling back to direct refresh) leaves the integration permanently broken until re-authentication.

[BUG] In sharing mode the sync endpoint's flat token response is passed to handleLarkError, which enforces Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope that the flat {access_token, expiry} response does not match, so the refresh throws. Every lark-calendar token refresh fails in sharing deployments, so Lark calendars stop working as soon as credential sync is configured.

[ADVISORY] The sync fetch never checks response.ok and sets no timeout or error handling, so a 4xx/5xx body from the endpoint is returned to callers and parsed as a token payload. A parent-app outage or misconfiguration surfaces as cryptic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" errors (or persisted garbage) across every synced app's booking path, and a hung endpoint stalls bookings until the fetch times out — the diff adds a hard runtime dependency on the parent app in the booking hot path.

[ADVISORY] The shipped payload contract is bespoke: the comment instructs deployers to "Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires", i.e. edit this file, because the feature only works for parent apps whose endpoint accepts exactly calcomUserId+appSlug form-encoded and returns the unspecified token JSON. Any parent app whose API differs forces self-hosters to patch Cal.com source and re-merge on every upgrade — the feature is incomplete as shipped and the response field names (expiry_date vs expires_in vs Lark's nested envelope) are undefined, so no single endpoint response can satisfy all ten integrated apps.

[ADVISORY] The entire credential-sync feature — the new webhook endpoint, refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and ten integration call-site rewrites — is added with no tests anywhere in the diff. The broken computed-key schema at line 8 and the Google SafeParseResult-wrapper storage bug would each have been caught by a single unit test; sharing-mode regressions across ten apps will reach production undetected.

[ADVISORY] The sharing-mode response validation (parseRefreshTokenResponse) is applied at only four of the ten refresh sites this PR rewires (google, office365-calendar, zoom, salesforce); msteams, hubspot, lark, webex, zoho-bigin and zohocrm receive sharing-mode responses with no validation at all. In sharing deployments a malformed endpoint response fails loudly for the validated apps but is persisted unvalidated for the other six, so the same parent-app bug produces inconsistent corruption across apps and is far harder to diagnose.

[ADVISORY] The handler calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse (throwing, not safeParse) on req.body for any HTTP method, and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) at lines 57-59 has no error handling, so invalid input escapes as unhandled exceptions. An authenticated caller sending a GET, a string userId, or undecryptable ciphertext gets an unhandled ZodError/decrypt exception and a 500 with stack details instead of a 4xx, leaving parent-app integrators debugging opaque server errors on a credential-writing endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint writes the decrypted keys to credential.key without validating them against the target app's credential schema (e.g. googleCredentialSchema), enforcing only that the app slug exists. A buggy parent app pushes malformed keys that Cal.com stores verbatim for any user and any app; the corruption surfaces later as confusing runtime crashes in the app's CalendarService instead of a 4xx at ingestion where the culprit is identifiable.

[ADVISORY] The webhook secret guarding this credential-writing endpoint is compared with plain !== string equality rather than a constant-time comparison. A network-adjacent attacker can attempt byte-wise timing recovery of the secret; once recovered, the holder can overwrite any user's credentials for any installed app.

[ADVISORY] process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY evaluates to its last operand, so the exported APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED constant's value is the raw encryption key string, not a boolean. Any code path that logs, serializes, or client-bundles this constant (constants.ts already mixes NEXT_PUBLIC_ client-facing values) leaks the credential encryption key; wrapping in Boolean(...) makes it safe.

[ADVISORY] The redirect URI replaces the config-driven appConfig.slug with the hardcoded literal "zoho-bigin", a change unrelated to credential sync that duplicates the slug outside config.json. The slug now lives in two places (config.json and this literal), so a slug change in config silently diverges add.ts from callback.ts and breaks the OAuth redirect; the edit is also untraceable churn inside a credential-sync PR.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) rather than the parsed token object, and this code persists that envelope directly as the credential key. On any install with credential sharing off, the first Google token refresh stores {success:true, data:{...}} as credential.key; the next getGoogleAuth runs googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), fails because access_token/refresh_token now sit one level deeper, and every Google Calendar operation throws until the user manually reconnects the app.

[BUG] Both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (z.string().toString() on a ZodString instance), so the schema declares only access_token plus an optional '[object Object]' property, and zod's default unknown-key stripping discards the expiry date and every other field the design says the sync endpoint returns. With sharing enabled, Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-263) and Zoom persist parsed data containing only access_token and the dummy refresh_token; expiry_date is never refreshed, stays in the past, and refreshAccessToken — a sync-endpoint HTTP call plus a credential DB write — runs on every single calendar operation.

[BUG] The sharing branch returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint while every call site was written against a provider-specific shape (gaxios res.data for Google, axios response.data for Zoho, the provider token object for Hubspot), so the function's return type changes at runtime with no adaptation at any call site. The untyped any return hides the mismatch from TypeScript: Google crashes on res?.data, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin crash on tokenInfo.data.error, Hubspot reads undefined token fields and persists NaN expiry, and Lark's handleLarkError rejects the non-Lark envelope — the credential-sync mode breaks every adapter it was built to enable.

[BUG] In sharing mode res is a raw fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar operation that triggers a token refresh dies with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)' inside refreshAccessToken; Google Calendar is entirely non-functional in the exact mode this PR adds.

[BUG] In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and the guard `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Zoho CRM calendar operations crash with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' on the first token refresh whenever credential sharing is enabled.

[BUG] In sharing mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Zoho Bigin calendar operations crash with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' on the first token refresh whenever credential sharing is enabled.

[BUG] BiginCalendarService passes `credentialId` — the credential row identifier — as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, which sends it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint, while every sibling call site passes credential.userId. The parent application receives the credential's database id where the contract (app-credential.ts: 'UserId of the cal.com user') requires the Cal.com user id, so it resolves the wrong user's tokens (or none) and the wrong user's credentials get synced back into this credential.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces a missing refresh_token with the literal sentinel string 'refresh_token', and callers persist that sentinel into the credential row. Office365's refresh (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-263) spreads the parsed data over the existing credentials, overwriting the user's real Microsoft refresh token with 'refresh_token'; the moment CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is unset or the parent app is unreachable, refreshOAuthTokens takes the local branch and sends refresh_token='refresh_token' to Microsoft, permanently bricking the credential.

[BUG] In sharing mode hubspotRefreshToken is a raw fetch Response assigned to HubspotToken, so expires_in and refresh_token are undefined when the unchanged downstream code reads them. The expiry computation yields Date.now() + undefined*1000 = NaN and the NaN-bearing token is persisted to the credential, so the stored Hubspot credential is corrupted (NaN expiry_date, no usable refresh_token) and Hubspot lookups fail from then on.

[BUG] The outbound sync fetch carries no authentication of any kind — no secret header, no signature — while the inbound webhook leg is protected by CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, leaving the integration's trust model one-sided. The parent app's endpoint must return live OAuth access tokens for an arbitrary calcomUserId to whatever process reaches it; nothing in this contract lets the parent distinguish Cal.com's request from any other network peer, so the endpoint hands out user access tokens unauthenticated.

[BUG] Salesforce's refresh never routes through the sync endpoint, but parseRefreshTokenResponse still switches to minimumTokenResponseSchema whenever the sharing env vars are set, stripping the Salesforce response down to access_token before it is persisted. The credential update stores {access_token, refresh_token} — instance_url, id, signature, issued_at are destroyed; on the next service construction the jsforce Connection is built without instanceUrl and every Salesforce API call fails, corrupting Salesforce credentials even though Salesforce was never part of the credential-sync flow.

[BUG] The webhook deduplicates with findFirst-then-create and no unique constraint on (userId, appId) backs the check. Two concurrent deliveries for the same user and app (a bulk push when the feature is switched on) both find no row and both insert, leaving duplicate credentials; every later webhook updates an arbitrary one of the duplicates via findFirst while the other drifts stale, and type-based credential resolution operates on both.

[ADVISORY] The SalesforceCalendarService constructor now performs an unconditional token refresh against login.salesforce.com plus a credential DB write on every instantiation, with no check that the stored access token is still valid. Every booking, availability check, and cancellation for a Salesforce-connected user pays a round trip to Salesforce's OAuth endpoint and a DB write — previously the constructor did no network I/O and jsforce refreshed lazily only on demand — adding latency and rate-limit exposure to a hot path.

[BUG] In sharing mode the Response handed to handleLarkError comes from the generic sync endpoint, whose documented contract is 'only the access token and expiry date', not Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the same junk string ('[object Object]', the second overwriting the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema implements neither the 'any numeric property is the expiry' rule nor 'allow other properties' - it is effectively z.object({access_token: z.string()}) that strips every other field from its parsed output. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, in sharing mode `safeParse(response)` will retain essentially only `access_token` (and possibly the junk key), discarding expiry fields and other token fields. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The header lookup uses process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME verbatim without lowercasing it, while Node lowercases all incoming header names. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The findFirst-then-create sequence runs without a transaction and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent syncs both take the create path, and the unordered findFirst thereafter updates a nondeterministic row. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The decrypted keys JSON is persisted as credential.key without any schema validation, so any decryptable-but-wrong payload (a string, null, or an object missing the app's required fields) is stored and acknowledged with 200 'Credentials updated'. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (ZodString does not override toString), so the second entry overwrites the first and the "minimum" schema requires only access_token — the intended "any property with a number is the expiry" validation does not exist. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The util unconditionally injects the literal string "refresh_token" as data.refresh_token whenever the parsed response lacks one — which is every response in sharing mode, since the sync endpoint returns only access token and expiry — and callers persist that value to the credential table. Every synced app's stored credential carries a fake refresh token; any downstream missing-refresh_token guard (e.g. zoom's) now passes on garbage, and if sharing is later disabled the direct-refresh path sends refresh_token="refresh_token" and the integration fails permanently until re-auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header — CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is never attached — even though the inbound webhook at apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts rejects callers without that same secret. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse bypasses salesforceTokenSchema and zod's default strip behavior reduces accessTokenParsed.data to {access_token} (plus the injected sentinel), so the credential update persists {access_token, refresh_token} and drops instance_url, signature, id, issued_at, scope and token_type. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, executes `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts).
