adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response that is assigned to the HubspotToken-typed variable, so .access_token, .refresh_token and .expires_in are all undefined when the new credential is computed and persisted. Hubspot stores a credential with undefined tokens and a NaN expiry_date, silently breaking the integration in sharing deployments with no error at refresh time — failures surface later as confusing 401s.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sharing mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), the function does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then (immediately after the shown diff context) computes expiry and updates credentials based on token fields. With a raw `Response`, `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token` / `refresh_token` / `expires_in` will be `undefined` at runtime unless the code explicitly parses JSON first (it doesn’t here), leading to persisting invalid/NaN-derived credential data in sharing deployments. This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips the zoom response to {access_token} plus the injected sentinel refresh_token:"refresh_token", and this stripped result is persisted as the credential key. The stored zoom credential loses token_type, scope and expires_in and carries a junk refresh token; if sharing is disabled or the endpoint removed, zoom refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" and the integration fails permanently until the user reinstalls the app.

adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` intentionally parses OAuth refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (only `access_token` plus a very limited set of other fields) and then *injects* `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it’s missing (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). Call sites then use this parsed output to update persisted credentials (e.g. Office365 merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and writes it back to Prisma; Google writes `key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` into Prisma). This can overwrite a real refresh token with the sentinel value and/or drop other token fields, creating persistent credential corruption consistent with the finding’s “junk refresh token / stripped fields” concern (even if the exact set of fields stripped depends on the schema).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The spread ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) merges the injected sentinel refresh_token:"refresh_token" over the credential's real refresh_token and the merged object is persisted via prisma.credential.update. In sharing mode every office365 refresh destroys the real refresh token in the DB; disabling sharing later (or a team credential with null userId falling back to direct refresh) leaves the integration permanently broken until re-authentication.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow now uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` and then explicitly injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it is missing. Immediately after, the code does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` and persists `o365AuthCredentials` via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This will overwrite the real stored `refresh_token` with the injected sentinel value whenever the sync endpoint returns no refresh_token (as the comments indicate it should), permanently breaking later non-sharing refresh paths until re-auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode the sync endpoint's flat token response is passed to handleLarkError, which enforces Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope that the flat {access_token, expiry} response does not match, so the refresh throws. Every lark-calendar token refresh fails in sharing deployments, so Lark calendars stop working as soon as credential sync is configured.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the token refresh now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and assigns its result to `resp`, which is then passed into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`. In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` set), `refreshOAuthTokens` does *not* call Lark; it instead `fetch`es `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and returns that response. The comments in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` say the sync endpoint response “should only contain the access token and expiry date” (i.e., a flat token response), which is incompatible with a Lark-specific error/response handler that (by design) expects Lark’s API response format. Thus, with credential sync configured, Lark refresh will route a non-Lark response through `handleLarkError`, causing refresh to fail and breaking Lark calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync fetch never checks response.ok and sets no timeout or error handling, so a 4xx/5xx body from the endpoint is returned to callers and parsed as a token payload. A parent-app outage or misconfiguration surfaces as cryptic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" errors (or persisted garbage) across every synced app's booking path, and a hung endpoint stalls bookings until the fetch times out — the diff adds a hard runtime dependency on the parent app in the booking hot path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), the “sync” path does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok`, without parsing JSON, and without any timeout/abort. Multiple call sites then treat the returned value as a token payload (or an axios/gaxios-style response): e.g. GoogleCalendarService does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` and then dereferences `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`—but a WHATWG `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and this will throw at runtime when syncing is enabled. Similar type/behavior mismatches exist in other integrations (e.g. Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object but would receive a `Response`). Separately, returning non-OK responses and/or hanging requests directly into the booking/token-refresh hot path matches the finding’s concern: errors surface as generic parse failures (e.g. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`) and there is no timeout handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The shipped payload contract is bespoke: the comment instructs deployers to "Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires", i.e. edit this file, because the feature only works for parent apps whose endpoint accepts exactly calcomUserId+appSlug form-encoded and returns the unspecified token JSON. Any parent app whose API differs forces self-hosters to patch Cal.com source and re-merge on every upgrade — the feature is incomplete as shipped and the response field names (expiry_date vs expires_in vs Lark's nested envelope) are undefined, so no single endpoint response can satisfy all ten integrated apps.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes a specific credential-sync request contract in `refreshOAuthTokens` (POSTing `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` via `URLSearchParams`) and explicitly tells deployers to edit Cal.com source: `// Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). The response contract is also intentionally loosened/underspecified when syncing is enabled (`parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to a minimal schema rather than each integration’s real schema), meaning the parent endpoint must “fit” multiple integrations without a clearly defined shared response shape. This is a diff-grounded product/architecture completeness concern (self-hosters needing to patch core code), not a single directly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire credential-sync feature — the new webhook endpoint, refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and ten integration call-site rewrites — is added with no tests anywhere in the diff. The broken computed-key schema at line 8 and the Google SafeParseResult-wrapper storage bug would each have been caught by a single unit test; sharing-mode regressions across ten apps will reach production undetected.

adjudication.rationale: Beyond the (true) “no tests added” point, the diff contains concrete defects: (1) `minimumTokenResponseSchema` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` tries to use computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluates to a single literal key (e.g. "[object Object]") rather than “any string key”, so the schema is effectively broken. (2) `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object, but `GoogleCalendarService` stores that wrapper directly into Prisma (`const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); ... data: { key }`), meaning it would persist `{success, data,...}` instead of the credential payload. These are real, diff-verifiable correctness issues that a unit test would likely catch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sharing-mode response validation (parseRefreshTokenResponse) is applied at only four of the ten refresh sites this PR rewires (google, office365-calendar, zoom, salesforce); msteams, hubspot, lark, webex, zoho-bigin and zohocrm receive sharing-mode responses with no validation at all. In sharing deployments a malformed endpoint response fails loudly for the validated apps but is persisted unvalidated for the other six, so the same parent-app bug produces inconsistent corruption across apps and is far harder to diagnose.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` for “sharing mode” validation but only wires it into some refresh paths: GoogleCalendar (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), Office365Calendar (`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), Zoom (`zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`), and Salesforce (`salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`). Other refresh sites modified to use `refreshOAuthTokens` (e.g., Hubspot, Lark, Webex, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM, Office365 video) do not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` in the shown diff. That creates an inconsistency in how refreshed-token payloads are shape-checked under sharing mode. However, the finding’s stronger claim that the other apps “receive sharing-mode responses with no validation at all” and that malformed responses are “persisted” isn’t fully verifiable from this diff alone (some flows may validate inside other helpers like `handleWebexResponse`, and persistence isn’t always shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse (throwing, not safeParse) on req.body for any HTTP method, and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) at lines 57-59 has no error handling, so invalid input escapes as unhandled exceptions. An authenticated caller sending a GET, a string userId, or undecryptable ciphertext gets an unhandled ZodError/decrypt exception and a 500 with stack details instead of a 4xx, leaving parent-app integrators debugging opaque server errors on a credential-writing endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does not gate on `req.method` (no POST-only check), so a GET/other method with missing/invalid body will still execute `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, which throws on invalid input. Additionally, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is executed without try/catch; invalid ciphertext or decrypt failures will throw and bubble as unhandled exceptions. Both paths can produce 500s instead of controlled 4xx responses, and this is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint writes the decrypted keys to credential.key without validating them against the target app's credential schema (e.g. googleCredentialSchema), enforcing only that the app slug exists. A buggy parent app pushes malformed keys that Cal.com stores verbatim for any user and any app; the corruption surfaces later as confusing runtime crashes in the app's CalendarService instead of a 4xx at ingestion where the culprit is identifiable.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse(...)`d and then written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` without any app-specific schema validation. The only gating is existence of the app slug via `appStoreMetadata[...]`, not that `keys` matches e.g. `googleCredentialSchema`/other credential schemas. This allows malformed/incorrect credential shapes to be persisted and later cause failures when downstream services assume a valid schema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook secret guarding this credential-writing endpoint is compared with plain !== string equality rather than a constant-time comparison. A network-adjacent attacker can attempt byte-wise timing recovery of the secret; once recovered, the holder can overwrite any user's credentials for any installed app.

adjudication.rationale: The new credential-writing webhook endpoint compares the provided secret using plain string inequality: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts). This is not a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`), so it can introduce a timing side-channel when validating a shared secret guarding a highly-privileged operation (writing/updating credentials).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY evaluates to its last operand, so the exported APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED constant's value is the raw encryption key string, not a boolean. Any code path that logs, serializes, or client-bundles this constant (constants.ts already mixes NEXT_PUBLIC_ client-facing values) leaks the credential encryption key; wrapping in Boolean(...) makes it safe.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`, which in JS evaluates to the last truthy operand (i.e., the **raw encryption key string**), not a boolean. The diff shows this constant being used as a boolean guard (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` and branching in `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`/`refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), so it will silently carry sensitive string data through the codebase. That creates a real risk of accidental leakage if this constant is ever logged/serialized or ends up in a client bundle, and it’s easily fixed by coercing to boolean (e.g., `Boolean(...)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect URI replaces the config-driven appConfig.slug with the hardcoded literal "zoho-bigin", a change unrelated to credential sync that duplicates the slug outside config.json. The slug now lives in two places (config.json and this literal), so a slug change in config silently diverges add.ts from callback.ts and breaks the OAuth redirect; the edit is also untraceable churn inside a credential-sync PR.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) rather than the parsed token object, and this code persists that envelope directly as the credential key. On any install with credential sharing off, the first Google token refresh stores {success:true, data:{...}} as credential.key; the next getGoogleAuth runs googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), fails because access_token/refresh_token now sit one level deeper, and every Google Calendar operation throws until the user manually reconnects the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (the `{ success, data, error }` envelope), not the parsed token payload. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That stores the envelope as `credential.key` instead of the credential object shape expected by `googleCredentialSchema` (previously it stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`), so subsequent reads/parses of `credential.key` as a credential payload would break due to fields being nested under `.data`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (z.string().toString() on a ZodString instance), so the schema declares only access_token plus an optional '[object Object]' property, and zod's default unknown-key stripping discards the expiry date and every other field the design says the sync endpoint returns. With sharing enabled, Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-263) and Zoom persist parsed data containing only access_token and the dummy refresh_token; expiry_date is never refreshed, stays in the past, and refreshAccessToken — a sync-endpoint HTTP call plus a credential DB write — runs on every single calendar operation.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, minimumTokenResponseSchema defines two computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately and become a single literal property name (very likely "[object Object]"), not an index signature. As a result the schema effectively only requires `access_token` and does not preserve fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, any real expiry field returned by the sync endpoint will be dropped from `refreshTokenResponse.data`. The calling code (e.g., office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials; zoom similarly uses it) would therefore persist credentials without a refreshed expiry, causing repeated refresh attempts and extra DB writes when the stored expiry remains stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sharing branch returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint while every call site was written against a provider-specific shape (gaxios res.data for Google, axios response.data for Zoho, the provider token object for Hubspot), so the function's return type changes at runtime with no adaptation at any call site. The untyped any return hides the mismatch from TypeScript: Google crashes on res?.data, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin crash on tokenInfo.data.error, Hubspot reads undefined token fields and persists NaN expiry, and Lark's handleLarkError rejects the non-Lark envelope — the credential-sync mode breaks every adapter it was built to enable.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns two incompatible runtime shapes depending on env: in the sharing branch it does `return response;` where `response` is a native `fetch` `Response` (apps-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), but in the normal branch it returns whatever the provider refresh function returns (gaxios `res` for Google, axios response for Zoho, a plain token object for Hubspot, etc.). Call sites are written against those provider-specific shapes and are not adapted for a `Response`: e.g. GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data` (expects gaxios-style `.data`), Zoho services read `tokenInfo.data...` (expects axios `.data`), Hubspot treats the return as `HubspotToken`, and Lark passes the result into `handleLarkError` expecting a Lark refresh response envelope. In credential-sync mode this will yield `undefined` fields / crashes or incorrect persistence, exactly as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode res is a raw fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar operation that triggers a token refresh dies with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)' inside refreshAccessToken; Google Calendar is entirely non-functional in the exact mode this PR adds.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code assumes `res` has an axios/gaxios-style `.data` (`const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token`). But `refreshOAuthTokens()` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object in sharing mode (`return response;` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`), which has no `.data`. This makes `token` undefined and will throw when accessing `token.access_token`, breaking token refresh (and thus Google Calendar operations) in the newly added sharing mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and the guard `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Zoho CRM calendar operations crash with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' on the first token refresh whenever credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, returns a raw `fetch(...)` Response (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is assigned from `await refreshOAuthTokens(async () => await axios(...), "zohocrm", credential.userId);` and then immediately dereferenced as `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. If sharing mode is enabled and the sync endpoint is set, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` will be a Fetch `Response` (no `.data`), so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` will throw a TypeError. This matches the reported crash scenario on token refresh in sharing mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Zoho Bigin calendar operations crash with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' on the first token refresh whenever credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow was changed to `const tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. Because `credentialId` (not `credential.userId`) is passed as the `userId` argument, that condition will likely be true and the function returns a `Response`, not an axios-like object with `.data`. The subsequent code `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` will then dereference `data` on a `Response`, causing `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BiginCalendarService passes `credentialId` — the credential row identifier — as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, which sends it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint, while every sibling call site passes credential.userId. The parent application receives the credential's database id where the contract (app-credential.ts: 'UserId of the cal.com user') requires the Cal.com user id, so it resolves the wrong user's tokens (or none) and the wrong user's credentials get synced back into this credential.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` treats that argument as `userId` and sends it to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (`body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug })`). Sibling call sites in the diff consistently pass `credential.userId` (e.g., Hubspot/Lark/Zoom/Webex). Given the contract in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` expects `userId` to be the Cal.com user id, passing a credential row id would cause the sync endpoint to resolve the wrong user (or none), leading to incorrect token refresh/sync behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces a missing refresh_token with the literal sentinel string 'refresh_token', and callers persist that sentinel into the credential row. Office365's refresh (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-263) spreads the parsed data over the existing credentials, overwriting the user's real Microsoft refresh token with 'refresh_token'; the moment CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is unset or the parent app is unreachable, refreshOAuthTokens takes the local branch and sends refresh_token='refresh_token' to Microsoft, permanently bricking the credential.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which mutates the successful parse result by setting `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the response lacks a refresh token (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). In Office365 refresh, the code now uses `const tokenResponse = parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema);` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` over existing credentials: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING is enabled and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates only a minimum schema (no refresh_token) and then injects the literal sentinel, which will overwrite the real stored `refresh_token` and then be persisted via `prisma.credential.update`. That can permanently break future local refresh flows which rely on the stored refresh token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode hubspotRefreshToken is a raw fetch Response assigned to HubspotToken, so expires_in and refresh_token are undefined when the unchanged downstream code reads them. The expiry computation yields Date.now() + undefined*1000 = NaN and the NaN-bearing token is persisted to the credential, so the stored Hubspot credential is corrupted (NaN expiry_date, no usable refresh_token) and Hubspot lookups fail from then on.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, executes a `fetch(...)` and **returns the raw `Response` object** (no `.json()` parsing) (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and does not adapt to `Response`, so in sharing mode `hubspotRefreshToken` will not have `expires_in` / `refresh_token` fields as expected. While the exact downstream expiry computation/persistence isn’t shown in this diff, the type/shape mismatch and missing parsing in sharing mode are directly verifiable and would break refresh handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The outbound sync fetch carries no authentication of any kind — no secret header, no signature — while the inbound webhook leg is protected by CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, leaving the integration's trust model one-sided. The parent app's endpoint must return live OAuth access tokens for an arbitrary calcomUserId to whatever process reaches it; nothing in this contract lets the parent distinguish Cal.com's request from any other network peer, so the endpoint hands out user access tokens unauthenticated.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, Cal.com makes a POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug })` and no authentication (no shared secret header, no signature, no bearer token, etc.). Meanwhile the inbound webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` explicitly enforces a secret via `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. The diff therefore introduces a one-sided trust model where the external "parent app" endpoint cannot distinguish Cal.com's sync request from any other caller, despite the contract implying it returns live access tokens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Salesforce's refresh never routes through the sync endpoint, but parseRefreshTokenResponse still switches to minimumTokenResponseSchema whenever the sharing env vars are set, stripping the Salesforce response down to access_token before it is persisted. The credential update stores {access_token, refresh_token} — instance_url, id, signature, issued_at are destroyed; on the next service construction the jsforce Connection is built without instanceUrl and every Salesforce API call fails, corrupting Salesforce credentials even though Salesforce was never part of the credential-sync flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the Salesforce refresh flow always fetches directly from Salesforce (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`) and then parses via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`. However `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema` whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`), regardless of whether the response actually came from the sync endpoint. That means when the sharing env vars + sync endpoint are configured, Salesforce’s full token response will be parsed/normalized by the minimum schema rather than `salesforceTokenSchema`, and the subsequent credential update (`data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }`) can drop Salesforce-specific fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`, `issued_at` that `salesforceTokenSchema` expects to preserve. This is consistent with corrupting stored Salesforce credentials even though Salesforce is not routed through `refreshOAuthTokens`/the sync endpoint in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook deduplicates with findFirst-then-create and no unique constraint on (userId, appId) backs the check. Two concurrent deliveries for the same user and app (a bulk push when the feature is switched on) both find no row and both insert, leaving duplicate credentials; every later webhook updates an arbitrary one of the duplicates via findFirst while the other drifts stale, and type-based credential resolution operates on both.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), credential persistence is implemented as `findFirst` (by `userId` + `appId`) followed by either `update` or `create`. This read-then-write sequence is not atomic and is vulnerable to concurrent requests: two deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no credential” and both proceed to `prisma.credential.create(...)`. Subsequent webhook calls again use `findFirst` and will update an arbitrary matching row, leaving other duplicates stale. The diff does not show any transaction/locking or `upsert`/unique-constraint-based enforcement to prevent this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The SalesforceCalendarService constructor now performs an unconditional token refresh against login.salesforce.com plus a credential DB write on every instantiation, with no check that the stored access token is still valid. Every booking, availability check, and cancellation for a Salesforce-connected user pays a round trip to Salesforce's OAuth endpoint and a DB write — previously the constructor did no network I/O and jsforce refreshed lazily only on demand — adding latency and rate-limit exposure to a hot path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new code refreshes the OAuth token via `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then immediately does `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no conditional check (e.g., access token expiry/validity) guarding this refresh/update, so every instantiation will incur a network round-trip and DB write. This is a concrete hot-path latency/rate-limit/architecture concern introduced by the diff, even if it may still be functionally correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode the Response handed to handleLarkError comes from the generic sync endpoint, whose documented contract is 'only the access token and expiry date', not Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope. The parsed body has no code field, so handleLarkError classifies every sync response as an API error and throws; Lark Calendar token refresh can never succeed under credential sharing.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, token refresh now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "lark-calendar", credential.userId)` and then unconditionally passes the returned `resp` into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) explicitly documents that in sharing mode it calls the generic `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and that "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date". That response will not be the Lark refresh endpoint’s expected shape, so routing it through `handleLarkError` (which is designed for Lark API responses) is incompatible and can break refresh under sharing mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-endpoint fetch has no timeout/AbortController and no fallback to the local refreshFunction when the endpoint fails or hangs. A slow or hung parent endpoint stalls every calendar and video operation for the nine wired apps for the fetch's default timeout window with no degradation path, where the pre-PR code refreshed directly against the provider — one flaky self-hoster endpoint takes down all bookings that touch those apps.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) replaces direct provider refresh with a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`. That fetch has no `AbortController`/timeout and no error handling; it just returns the response promise. Multiple integrations now call this helper (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Webex/etc.), so a slow/hung sync endpoint can stall token refresh paths with no built-in degradation or fallback to `refreshFunction()` on endpoint failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The credential lookup filters on appId, which is NULL on credentials created before the appId column existed or via any create path that doesn't set it, so those rows are invisible to the webhook. For a user who already connected the app through Cal.com's own OAuth flow, the webhook takes the create branch and inserts a second credential of the same type; type-based credential resolution then sees the same account twice and booking flows create duplicate events and duplicate availability lookups.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, the existing credential is located only via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and the update path depends on finding that row. The diff does not show guarantees that all pre-existing credentials (created before this webhook existed or via other paths) always have `appId` populated, so this lookup could miss an existing credential and fall through to `prisma.credential.create(...)`, creating duplicates. However, the claim that older rows have `appId = NULL` and that type-based resolution elsewhere will then cause duplicated bookings is not directly verifiable from the diff (no schema/migration history or resolution logic shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Refresh success is gated on response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok/response.status. Any proxy or HTTP/2 hop that normalizes or strips the reason phrase makes statusText '' and every Salesforce refresh throws HttpError 400 despite a valid token response, breaking Salesforce for users behind such intermediaries.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data, error}) instead of the parsed data, and GoogleCalendarService persists that envelope directly as credential.key, replacing the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) value. On the first token refresh on any install (credential sharing disabled included), prisma.credential.update stores {success:true,data:{...},error:null} as the key; the next service load reads credential.key.access_token/refresh_token as undefined and Google auth fails, breaking Google Calendar for every user until they re-authenticate.
matched_golden_ids: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse envelope and the service persists that envelope as credential.key instead of the parsed token payload (data) / using schema.parse, leading to undefined access_token/refresh_token on reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites the parsed output's refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the schema result lacks it, and callers spread that data over the live credentials before persisting (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 does {...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}). With credential sharing enabled the minimum schema strips the real refresh_token, the literal replaces the user's actual refresh_token in the persisted credential, and the next refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token", which the provider rejects — the integration is permanently broken until re-auth, and for rotating providers like Zoom the newly issued refresh token is stripped and lost outright.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after a successful parse it does `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`, which fabricates a literal refresh token when the refresh response omits one. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the returned parsed data is spread onto the live credentials (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`), so when the provider does not return `refresh_token` on refresh, the placeholder overwrites the previously valid stored refresh token and will break subsequent refreshes. This is a correctness/data-loss issue introduced by the new helper and its usage pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns the provider-native result in the fallback branch but a raw, never-.json()-parsed fetch Response in the sharing branch, while its eight call sites consume provider-specific shapes (gaxios .data, axios .data, HubSpot client token objects, Lark/Webex/Zoom Response handlers). In sharing mode every non-fetch caller crashes or corrupts credentials (see the google/hubspot/zoho sites), and even the Response-consuming callers require the single CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT to return each provider's exact body shape, contradicting the code's own comment that the response "should only contain the access token and expiry date" — e.g. Lark's handleLarkError expects {code, data:{access_token, expires_in}} and fails on the documented flat shape.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sharing branch returns a native `fetch(...)` `Response`, while the fallback branch returns whatever the provider SDK returns (`axios` response object, HubSpot token object, gaxios response, etc.). Multiple call sites clearly expect provider-native shapes, not a `Response`: e.g. Google Calendar now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which will be `undefined` for a `fetch` `Response` (no `.data`) and thus corrupt/throw when accessing token fields. HubSpot assigns the result to `HubspotToken` (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`), and Zoho uses it like an axios result (`tokenInfo.data...` in `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`), both incompatible with a `fetch` `Response` in sharing mode. Additionally, the comment in `refreshOAuthTokens` says the endpoint “should only contain the access token and expiry date”, but several consumers (e.g. Lark’s `handleLarkError(resp, ...)` expecting Lark-shaped JSON in `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) would break if given that documented flat shape, confirming the inconsistency is real and introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode res is a fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar operation with sharing enabled crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token')" inside refreshAccessToken, failing the booking instead of refreshing the token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` and then reads `token.access_token`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch(...)` `Response` object when sharing is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), and a `Response` has no `.data` property. That makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime when sharing mode is on, matching the reported crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] hubspotRefreshToken is annotated HubspotToken but in sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so every field access (refresh_token, access_token, expires_in) yields undefined. HubSpot sharing-mode refresh computes a NaN expiryDate and persists a credential whose token fields are all undefined, silently killing the integration on the next API call while the type annotation hides the mismatch from the compiler.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens` may return a `fetch` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see new `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). However the call site assigns its return value to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In sharing mode this will be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, so any later accesses like `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token`, `expires_in`, `refresh_token`, etc. will be `undefined`/invalid at runtime while the TypeScript annotation masks the mismatch. The diff does not show any JSON parsing/conversion for the HubSpot sharing-mode path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode tokenInfo is a fetch Response with no .data property, so tokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError. Every Zoho Bigin calendar operation with sharing enabled crashes at "if (!tokenInfo.data.error)" instead of refreshing the token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is now obtained via `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. That helper returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). A `Response` does not have an Axios-style `.data` property, but the Zoho Bigin code still does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`, which will throw a TypeError in sharing mode. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response with no .data property, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError. Every Zoho CRM calendar operation with sharing enabled crashes at "if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)" instead of refreshing the token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns a `fetch(...)` Response object. In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is assigned from `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately accessed as `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. If sharing mode is enabled and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` will be a fetch `Response` (no `.data`), causing a runtime `TypeError` at `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys both evaluate to the duplicate literal "[object Object]" (z.string().toString() is "[object Object]"), so the second entry overwrites the first and the promised "any property with a number is the expiry" validation does not exist. In sharing mode the schema validates only access_token; responses with no expiry field pass validation, expiry_date/expires_in are never persisted, and every calendar operation re-runs the refresh flow (a per-operation POST to the sync endpoint) because the stored token always appears expired.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines two computed keys using `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()`. Those are runtime string keys, and both evaluate to the same string (effectively `"[object Object]"`), so the latter overwrites the former. As a result, the schema does not enforce “any numeric expiry field” at all and (because Zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default) it will also drop fields like `expiry_date` / `expires_in` from the returned `.data` in sharing mode. This matches the finding that sharing-mode validation degenerates to essentially just `access_token` and can fail to persist expiry information.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When credential sharing is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse applies minimumTokenResponseSchema to Salesforce's response (Salesforce never uses the sync endpoint itself), and z.object's default key-stripping reduces accessTokenParsed.data to {access_token}, so the persisted key loses instance_url, id, signature, scope and token_type. Enabling credential sharing for other apps corrupts every Salesforce credential on its next refresh: the stored key no longer carries instance_url, so the next jsforce.Connection hits the default login domain and API calls fail for customers on My Domain instances.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse` the choice of schema is gated only on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, not on the app being refreshed. Salesforce refresh (`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`) calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`, so if credential sharing is enabled for any reason and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, it will validate with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of `salesforceTokenSchema`. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, the parsed `accessTokenParsed.data` will drop Salesforce fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`, `scope`, `token_type`, and the code then persists `{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ... }`, overwriting the credential key without those fields. This is a verifiable data-loss/breakage path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId where every other call site passes credential.userId, so the sync endpoint receives the credential row id as calcomUserId. In sharing mode the parent app cannot map the request to a user (it gets a credential id, not the cal.com user id the sync contract documents), so Bigin token sync returns tokens for the wrong entity or none at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. But `refreshOAuthTokens`’s signature is `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)` and, in sharing mode, it sends that value as `calcomUserId` in the POST body (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). Other updated call sites consistently pass `credential.userId` (e.g. Hubspot/Lark/Office365/Zoom/Webex), so using a credential row id here would break the expected contract and prevent correct user mapping at the sync endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook selects an arbitrary credential row via findFirst on {userId, appId} with no ordering and no way to target a specific credential, then overwrites its key. A user with multiple credentials for the same app (multiple connected accounts, which Cal supports) has an unpredictable one overwritten by the parent app's push, silently destroying the other account's tokens; bookings on the clobbered account then fail with auth errors.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts), the code looks up an existing credential with `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and, if found, updates that single row’s `key`. There is no `orderBy` and no way for the webhook payload to specify which credential to update (e.g., by credential id or external account identifier). If the data model allows multiple credentials for the same `{userId, appId}` (common for “multiple connected accounts”), this will update an arbitrary matching row and can overwrite the wrong account’s tokens/keys, causing data loss/unpredictable behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds an ungated Salesforce token refresh (fetch + statusText check + credential write) that runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, where previously jsforce refreshed lazily only when the stored access token was rejected. Every Salesforce booking/availability check on every install (no feature flag, contrary to the PR's opt-in sync objective) now pays a login.salesforce.com round-trip plus a DB write, and a Salesforce outage or transient network failure fails operations that previously succeeded with the valid stored token; the response.statusText !== "OK" check also throws HttpError 400 behind proxies that strip HTTP reason phrases.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token exchange against `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` plus a `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (i.e., executed whenever this code path runs), with no gating on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` or `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. This is a behavioral regression vs. a lazy/only-on-failure refresh strategy: it introduces a network dependency and DB write into the normal path and can fail operations during transient Salesforce/network issues even if the stored token remains valid. Additionally, the error check `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is brittle (reason phrases may be empty/modified by proxies); `response.ok`/`response.status` should be used, so this can incorrectly throw `HttpError(400)` despite a non-error response semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-endpoint fetch sends no authentication of any kind (no secret, no header) and consumes the response as plaintext tokens, while the inbound webhook path encrypts the same keys with AES-256. Anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can POST {calcomUserId, appSlug} and receive live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary users, and the tokens cross the wire with no application-layer encryption — contradicting the confidentiality posture the inbound encryption establishes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the new credential-sync path (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication/secret header. By contrast, the inbound webhook endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) enforces a shared secret header and expects AES-encrypted payloads. However, the finding’s claim that “anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can … receive live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary users” can’t be verified from this diff because the security/behavior of that external endpoint isn’t part of the PR. What is verifiable is the inconsistency and lack of an auth mechanism in the outbound sync request, which is a concrete design/security concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refactor replaces safeParse-plus-log-and-continue with parseRefreshTokenResponse's hard throw, deleting the previous tolerance for MS schema drift along with the console.error diagnostics (zodError + MS response) and leaving the following tokenResponse.success check as dead code. An MS response that fails refreshTokenResponseSchema (schema drift, transient error body) previously logged and let the operation proceed with existing credentials; it now throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" and fails the live booking, with no error context left for operators to diagnose.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and on failure only `console.error(...)` (logging zodError + MS response) while continuing with the existing `o365AuthCredentials` and updating Prisma. The refactor replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `safeParse` fails, and the prior console diagnostics are removed. Also, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure, downstream checks like `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` in Office365 are effectively dead/pointless (success will always be true if it returns). The finding’s claims about stricter failure behavior and loss of logging are directly supported by the diff; the impact on “live booking” is plausible but not provable solely from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler uses schema.parse (which throws ZodError) plus unguarded symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse and has no HTTP method check, so malformed or GET requests surface as unhandled 500s. Parent-app integrators sending a slightly wrong payload (string userId, missing keys, wrong encryption) get opaque 500 responses leaking server error details instead of a 4xx validation message, and cannot distinguish their bug from an outage.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, there is no HTTP method guard (so GET/other methods reach `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`), and both `zod.parse(...)` and the subsequent `symmetricDecrypt(...)` + `JSON.parse(...)` are unguarded. Any malformed body (e.g., missing/invalid types like string `userId`), invalid ciphertext, or bad/empty encryption key will throw and surface as an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response. This behavior is directly visible in the handler implementation and matches the finding’s claim about opaque 500s for slightly wrong payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined as process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which evaluates to the raw AES encryption key string, not a boolean. A developer debugging credential sync who logs or serializes the flag-named constant (the natural move for an *_ENABLED flag) writes the credential encryption key into logs, and any future `=== true` comparison silently reads the feature as disabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`, which in JS evaluates to the second operand (the raw `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` string) when both env vars are set, not a boolean. That means the exported “*_ENABLED” flag can carry and expose the encryption key value if logged/serialized, and it is also type-incorrect for an enabled flag (e.g., any strict boolean checks would fail). This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff introduces three behavior-bearing modules (parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens, the app-credential webhook) with zero tests, leaving the persisted-credential shape and the sharing/fallback branch selection unpinned. The envelope-vs-data return bug that corrupts Google credentials and the "refresh_token" literal that destroys refresh tokens shipped precisely because no test pinned what prisma.credential.update stores; regressions here surface as runtime OAuth breakage across every calendar/video app, not as CI failures.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces verifiable broken behavior. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` is used as `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `success`/`data`), not the parsed credential payload, so this would store an envelope instead of the credential shape. Separately, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` Response when syncing is enabled, but callers like Google still read `res?.data` (a pattern for axios/google client responses), which a `fetch` Response does not have, yielding undefined tokens. Also `parseRefreshTokenResponse` mutates missing `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token", and call sites like Office365 merge `tokenResponse.data` into existing credentials, potentially overwriting a real refresh token with the placeholder. These are concrete correctness/data-loss risks shown directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The credential-sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication of any kind — no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, no signature, no auth header — even though this endpoint's documented purpose is to return live OAuth access tokens for the named user. The parent application has no way to verify the request came from its Cal.com instance, so the token-issuing endpoint must either accept unauthenticated requests — letting anyone who can reach it POST any calcomUserId/appSlug pair and receive that user's live access tokens — or the operator must invent an undocumented out-of-band scheme (e.g. secret-in-URL); the shared secret that guards the reverse webhook direction is never applied to this direction.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the code `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no auth headers, signature, or inclusion of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. The stored Office365 credential's real refresh_token is replaced by the placeholder string and the stale expiry_date is kept (the expiry field was stripped by the broken schema), so the next refresh POSTs refresh_token=refresh_token to Microsoft and fails permanently; disabling credential sharing later does not bring the lost token back.

adjudication.rationale: In Office365 refresh, the code now calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges the parsed data into the existing credential (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`) before persisting via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. In sharing mode, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not require/retain `refresh_token`) and then forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the placeholder string when missing: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. That placeholder is then spread over and overwrites the real stored refresh token, permanently losing it. Since the minimum schema also may not retain the real expiry field(s), the old expiry can remain. Disabling sharing later would not restore the lost refresh token, so subsequent non-sharing refreshes would fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When credential sharing is enabled, Salesforce's own full token response is parsed with minimumTokenResponseSchema, and the credential.update persists {...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token}, which now contains only access_token and refresh_token. instance_url, signature, id, issued_at, scope and token_type are silently deleted from the stored salesforce credential; the next service construction builds the jsforce.Connection without instance_url and every Salesforce calendar operation fails, with the dropped fields unrecoverable without re-auth. adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is truthy *and* `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, it ignores the app-specific schema and instead validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). Salesforce now calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` and then persists `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }` (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts). Under the sharing+endpoint configuration, this can cause Salesforce’s refreshed token payload to be reduced to only the “minimum” shape, dropping fields that `salesforceTokenSchema` would otherwise preserve (e.g., `instance_url`, `signature`, etc.), resulting in irreversible credential data loss until re-auth. The finding slightly overstates the trigger (it also requires `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), but the core data-loss risk is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but all nine callers treat the return value as the provider-specific response shape they had before. adjudication.rationale:

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] zoho-bigin passes credentialId (the credential row's id) as the userId parameter of refreshOAuthTokens, which becomes the calcomUserId sent to the sync endpoint. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a constant string ("[object Object]"), with the second entry overwriting the first, so the schema is really {access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown} — not the documented 'any numeric property is the expiry' wildcard — and z.object strips every unknown key. Since `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default (no `.passthrough()`), in credential-sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the parse result will drop fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and any other token fields, leaving only `access_token`. The helper then injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever it’s missing, which can overwrite/propagate a literal placeholder refresh token via call sites that merge/persist `tokenResponse.data` (e.g., Office365 merges `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials; Zoom similarly now uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response but the code reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` expecting the axios response shape, and Response.data is undefined, so the property access throws TypeError. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode tokenInfo is the sync endpoint's fetch Response but the code reads `tokenInfo.data.error` expecting the axios response shape, and Response.data is undefined, so the access throws TypeError. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential's DB id) as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter — which is serialized as `calcomUserId` in the sync request — while every other app passes credential.userId. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler validates the body with throwing `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (not safeParse) and no try/catch, so any malformed body — or any GET, whose body is undefined — throws ZodError out of the handler. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse on the keys payload are unguarded, so a payload encrypted with a mismatched CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or corrupt ciphertext) throws inside the handler. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout (and no response.ok check) and sits on the token-refresh path of every calendar/video operation in sharing mode. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sharing mode is enabled it calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no AbortSignal/timeout and no `response.ok` / status handling, then returns the raw `Response`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse returns data reduced to {access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"} (the broken minimum schema strips the rest and injects the placeholder), and this spread overwrites o365AuthCredentials' real refresh token before the credential update persists it. adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` which (a) does not include `refresh_token` and (b) is a plain `z.object(...)` (so unknown keys like expiry fields are stripped). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse applies the stripping minimum schema to the sync response, so parsedToken.data is {access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"} with no expires_in, and the code that follows persists that as the Zoom credential key. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to the stripping minimum schema whenever the sharing env flags are set, but Salesforce's refresh never goes through the sync endpoint — it always parses Salesforce's real response — so the persisted key keeps only {access_token, refresh_token} and loses instance_url, signature, scope and token_type.
